From the owner
Most custom homes in Visalia, Tulare, Hanford and Fresno take 12 to 18 months from the first design meeting to move-in. Construction itself is only 8 to 12 months of that - the rest is design, engineering and permitting before anyone breaks ground. Realistic 2026 permit timelines: 8 to 12 weeks in the City of Visalia, 6 to 10 weeks in Tulare and Hanford, and 10 to 16 weeks in unincorporated Tulare County when a well and septic are involved. Two things quietly add weeks after the permit is issued. A change order after framing runs about two weeks once you re-engineer, redo the runs, and repaint. A failed rough inspection costs 5 to 10 business days waiting on the next slot. Rural PG&E service extensions often add 6 to 14 weeks beyond the original quote, so apply the day you close on the land. The best schedule move is unglamorous: pick cabinets, tile, flooring and fixtures during design, before the permit is issued. Our full phase-by-phase breakdown includes a realistic 14-month schedule for a 2,500 sq ft Visalia build.

Florida law requires impact windows, doors and shutters to carry state product approval, tested to state standards, before they go in. In Broward and Miami-Dade they must also meet High Velocity Hurricane Zone standards, a stricter rating that applies here. Shutters and most window or door replacements need a permit. The inspector checks that the product matches its approval and went in the way the manufacturer says. If it doesn't match, it doesn't pass. Before any deposit: find the Florida product approval on the label, or search the Florida Building Commission product approval database. Then ask your contractor: "Who applies for the permit, and when?" Good answer: they do, before install. Label or permit: which one have you checked?

From the owner
A small roofing problem in the fall can become much more troublesome once winter weather arrives. Missing shingles, deteriorating flashing, clogged gutters, and damaged seals can allow moisture to enter vulnerable parts of your roofing system. Freezing temperatures may complicate repairs, while snow and ice can make roof access more difficult and increase safety risks. In some homes, ice dams develop when heat escapes into the roof area, melts snow, and allows water to refreeze near colder roof edges. The resulting water can sometimes back up beneath roofing materials and contribute to interior leaks. Before winter sets in, look for visible signs of deterioration from a safe location and arrange a professional inspection if you have concerns. Check for water stains on ceilings, damaged shingles, loose flashing, and gutters blocked by leaves or debris. Adequate attic insulation, ventilation, and drainage can also play important roles in winter roof performance. Do not climb onto an icy roof or attempt dangerous snow removal yourself. Renovate Right, Inc. can help homeowners evaluate roofing concerns and explore appropriate repair or renovation options. Addressing problems early can help reduce the chance of unexpected leaks during severe weather. Contact Renovate Right, Inc. today to discuss your roof's condition and plan the maintenance or repairs needed to help protect your home throughout winter.

Water damage in a bathroom rarely stays small. In Tyler, TX, a slow leak behind tile or under a vanity can lead to mold, soft subfloors, and damaged framing within weeks. Watch for warning signs: musty odors, peeling paint, loose tile, or stains on the ceiling below. The faster you find the source and dry the area, the less you'll replace. Restoration usually means removing affected materials, treating for mold, fixing the leak, and rebuilding with waterproof systems so it doesn't return. If you suspect damage, don't wait—call us for an assessment.
